cards.title: What is on the plate
cards.idea: A balanced meal on a thali carries different foods that do different jobs inside you.

interaction.prompt: Tap each item on the thali to see what job it does

cards.reveal: Rice and roti give energy, dal and paneer build the body, sabzi and salad keep you healthy. Different foods, different jobs.

imageSpec.subject: an Indian steel thali with rice, dal, roti, sabzi and salad
imageSpec.caption: One thali, many nutrients

cards.title: The five workers
cards.idea: Food is made of nutrients. Each nutrient class does one main job: energy, building, protecting.

interaction.prompt: Match each nutrient to the job you think it does

cards.reveal: Carbohydrates and fats give energy, proteins build and repair, vitamins and minerals protect and regulate.

interaction.prompt: Drag carbohydrate to the job it does

stages.reveal: Carbohydrates are the body's main fuel for daily activity.
stages.caption: Rice and roti keep you running.

stages.reveal: Proteins build muscles and repair worn-out parts. Dal, paneer, egg and fish are rich in protein.
stages.caption: Proteins are the body's bricks.

cards.title: Energy in food
cards.idea: Different foods release different amounts of energy, measured in kilocalories.

interaction.prompt: Slide to change how much rice you eat and watch the energy

cards.reveal: More rice means more energy taken in. Energy scales with the amount eaten.

breakpoint.revelation: at zero grams there is no food, so no energy enters the body; energy cannot be negative

cards.title: Deficiency diseases
cards.idea: When a nutrient is missing for a long time, the body shows a deficiency disease.

interaction.prompt: Tap a missing nutrient to see what happens

cards.reveal: No vitamin C causes scurvy, no vitamin D or calcium causes weak bones, no iron causes anaemia, no protein causes wasting.

cards.title: How plants eat
cards.idea: Green plants make their own food from sunlight, water and carbon dioxide by photosynthesis.

interaction.prompt: Tap the leaf, sun, water and air to build the recipe

cards.reveal: Leaves use chlorophyll to trap sunlight and combine water and carbon dioxide into glucose, releasing oxygen. This is autotrophic nutrition.

imageSpec.subject: a green leaf with sunlight arrows, water rising from roots and carbon dioxide entering
imageSpec.caption: Plants: the only kitchen that runs on light

steps.note: raw ingredients air and water become food and oxygen
balanced: six molecules each of carbon dioxide and water make one glucose

cards.title: Two ways to eat
cards.idea: Plants make food (autotrophs); animals must take food from outside (heterotrophs).

interaction.prompt: Tap to reveal the two kinds of nutrition

cards.reveal: Autotrophic nutrition builds food from simple raw materials. Heterotrophic nutrition takes ready-made food from plants or other animals.

chapters.title: The balanced plate
chapters.script: Picture your thali. Rice and roti give carbohydrates for energy. Dal and paneer give protein to build and repair. Sabzi and fruit give vitamins and minerals to protect you. A meal with all of these in the right amount is a balanced diet.

chapters.title: When nutrients go missing
chapters.script: Leave out a nutrient too long and the body complains. No vitamin C brings scurvy. Too little iron brings anaemia. Weak protein means poor growth. This is why variety on the plate matters more than any single food.

chapters.title: Plants and animals
chapters.script: Plants are autotrophs. Using chlorophyll they trap sunlight and turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose, giving out oxygen. Animals and humans are heterotrophs; we cannot make food, so we eat plants or other animals. Two paths, one goal: energy and building blocks for life.

options: Too much energy stored as fat

boss.prompt: In photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and water and release the gas ________.
Why is a mango tree called an autotroph but a goat a heterotroph?
options: The tree makes its own food while the goat must eat plants
The tree needs no water but the goat does
The goat makes food from sunlight but the tree cannot
Both make their own food equally
boss.answer: The tree makes its own food while the goat must eat plants
